description.value: Lorna Lake sits inside South Chilcotin Mountains Park, a staffed-facility-free wilderness zone with no potable water, frequent grizzly activity, and rapidly changing alpine weather — every visitor must be fully self-sufficient and filter water from the lake or streams. The payoff is a spectacular high-country setting with 200+ km of trails connecting broad valleys, alpine meadows, and mountain ridges.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The OSM record contains only two tags (tourism=camp_site, name) with no address or contact details. The website URL points to the broader South Chilcotin Mountains Park BC Parks page rather than a Lorna Lake-specific page; this page confirms the park is a genuine wilderness area with no staffed facilities or regular ranger patrols. The only definitive amenity determination from the website is an explicit denial of potable water: 'Bring your own drinking water as potable water is not available in the park.'
concerns: Website URL resolves to the broader South Chilcotin Mountains Park page and does not name or describe Lorna Lake Wilderness Campground specifically; no campground-level details (site count, reservation status, specific facilities) are available.
OSM record is extremely sparse with only name and tourism=camp_site tags; no address, phone, or contact details present.
URL was auto-discovered rather than sourced directly from OSM tags; although discovery confidence is rated high, the park page does not mention Lorna Lake by name.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: A legitimate BC Parks wilderness campground within a park that explicitly supports mountain biking; a meaningful listing for self-sufficient off-road or bikepacking tourers in the South Chilcotin region.
enrichment_extras.notes: Mountain biking is explicitly listed as a permitted and supported activity within South Chilcotin Mountains Park. The park is remote (approximately 150km north of Whistler) and this campground is best suited to self-sufficient bikepacking or off-road touring cyclists rather than road tourers.

wow_evidence: South Chilcotin Mountains Park… 200+ km of trails… mountain biking
